Complainant

R/o. 1482A, Wazir Nagar,
Kotla Mubarakpur,

Judgment:
1. The present is a complaint filed under section 16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954
(Pfa Act), alleging that the accused has violated the provisions of the Pfa Act and Rules.

The
acc
used Mittarsain Gupta is stated to be the vendor-cum-proprietor of M/s Anupam Sweets, from where the food article, that is, 'Boondi Ke Laddu' was lifted for sampling.

2. As per the complaint, on 02.11.2007, the food officials consisting of Food Inspector (FI) Ashok Kumar Singh and Field Assistant (FA) Satish Kumar Gaur under the supervision of Local Health Authority (LHA)/SDM Sh. Vishwendra reached along with their staff at the premises of M/s.
Anupam Sweets at Shop No.1, Sector 12, R.K.Puram, New Delhi-110022, where the accused was found conducting the business of various food articles, which were lying stored for sale for human consumption.
The FI disclosed his identity and expressed his intention to purchase a sample of Boondi Ke Laddu from the vendor lying in an open tray bearing no label declaration, to which he agreed.
The sample was then lifted as per procedure prescribed under the PFA Act and Rules.
Each sample was separately packed, fastened, marked and sealed and necessary documents were prepared at the spot, including the Notice as per Form-VI, panchnama, etc.
The price of sample was paid to the vendor.
Thereafter, one counterpart of the sample was sent to the Public Analyst (PA) in intact condition and the other two counterparts were deposited with SDM/LHA.

Vide report dated 07.12.2007, the PA found the sample to be not conforming to the standards of Vanaspati declared as In Re vs Mittarsain Gupta on 20 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71684138/
1

sentences.text: an ingredient on the ground that it gave negative Baudouin Test.
Upon receipt of report, the SDM/LHA ordered investigation which was carried out by FI.

After completion of investigation,
sanction under section 20 of the PFA Act was obtained from the Director PFA.
The complaint was then filed in the court on 30.04.2008 alleging violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act, as punishable section 7/16(1)(a) of PFA Act.
3. As the complaint was filed in writing by a public servant, recording of pre-summoning evidence was dispensed with and the accused was summoned vide order dated 30.04.2008.

The accused appeared but never filed application under section 13(2) of PFA Act thereby exercising his right to get the second counterpart of the sample to be analysed from Central Food Laboratory (CFL).

4. Based on the report of the PA, notice of accusation under section 251 CrPC was framed against the accused on 01.12.2009 for commission of the offence punishable under section 7/16(1)(a) PFA Act,
being violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act, to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
5. At the trial, prosecution initially examined three witnesses in support of its case.
PW-1 FI A.K.Singh, PW-2 SDM/LHA Sh. Vishwendra and PW-3 FA Satish Kumar Gaur were part of the team that had visited the spot for sample proceedings.

All these witnesses deposed about the proceedings conducted by them on 02.11.2007 and narrated the steps undertaken by them during the sample proceedings, including disclosing their identity, expressing intention to purchase sample for analysis, lifting the sample of 1500 gms Boondi Ke Laddu lying in an open tray bearing no label declaration, breaking it into smallest possible pieces, mixing/ homogenizing it, dividing it in three parts and putting in clean and dry bottles, adding 40 drops of formalin in each bottle as preservative, fastening, sealing, marking the sample bottles, and obtaining signatures of vendor and witnesses.

They also proved the necessary documents including the vendor's receipt Ex. PW-1/A,
Notice Ex. PW- 1/B, Panchnama Ex. PW-1/C, Report under Rule 9(e) Ex. PW-1/C-1, PA Receipt Ex.
PW-1/D and LHA receipt Ex. PW-1/E.
PA report Ex. PW-1/F was received and investigation was started.
Letter Ex. PW-1/G was written to the vendor and reply Ex. PW-1/G-1 was received.
Vendor also sent two replies Ex. PW-1/G-1 and Ex. PW-1/G-2.

A letter Ex. PW-1/H was written to STO,
Ward no. 101 and its reply was received.
Letter Ex. PW-1/I was written to MCD but it was not replied.
After completion of investigation, sanction Ex. PW-1/J was taken from the Director PFA and the complaint Ex. PW-1/K was filed in the court.

A copy of PA report with intimation letter Ex.
PW-1/L was sent to the accused vide postal receipt Ex. PW-1/M.
These witnesses were duly cross-examined by Ld. Defence Counsel wherein they denied that the sampling method was not proper or that the accused had been falsely implicated.

They could not state if the sesamol content get degraded when the food article used to be fried at high temperature of 180-200 degree Celsius which results in the Baudouin Test giving negative result.
6. Statement of the accused under section 313 CrPC was initially recorded on 22.09.2015 wherein he denied the allegations and pleaded innocence.

Though he admitted the proceedings dated 02.11.2007, yet he questioned the PA report on the ground that the BT Test gives negative result when the Vanaspati is heated at high temperature which destroys the sesamol content of til oil.

He chose to lead evidence in defence, he summoned some record from the complainant department but In Re vs Mittarsain Gupta on 20 March, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71684138/
2

sentences.text: it was reported that the said record was not traceable.
As such, no defence evidence was led.
7. After hearing the matter, vide order dated 16.12.2016, this court was of the view that the evidence of Public Analyst who had analyzed the sample and gave report was necessary.
As such, the said Public Analyst was summoned as a witness.
8. PA Smt. Mohini Shrivastava who had given report Ex. PW-1/F was examined as PW-4 to clarify the position.
She deposed that the BT Test was conducted to determine the presence of sesame oil (til oil) in Vanaspati which is mandatory to be added as per PFA Rules.

During cross-examination,
she accepted that no standards have been prescribed for Boondi Ke Laddu and the sample was considered as a proprietary food.
She accepted that upon heating at high temperature of Vanaspati or any food article prepared from Vanaspati, the sesamol content gets degraded due to which BT Test might give negative result.
She also admitted that this view has been documented in the book by David Pearson which is a standard recognized literature in the field.

9. In view of her evidence, additional statement of accused under Section 313 CrPC was recorded on 20.03.2017 wherein the accused reiterated that the food article used to be prepared by frying the main ingredients at a high temperature due to which the til oil containing sesamol gets destroyed, as a result of which the Baudouin test gives negative result.
He chose not to lead further evidence in defence.

10. It is in these circumstances, Ld. SPP for the complainant has argued that the complainant has been able to establish its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt, on the ground that the accused has not been able to rebut the findings of the PA report dated 07.12.2007.
It is submitted that all the witnesses have supported its case and no major contradiction can be seen in their testimony.
11. On the other hand, Ld. Defence Counsel has submitted that the sample proceedings were not conducted properly and that there are various missing links in the testimony of witnesses.

Ld.
Counsel has strongly contended that there is no standard for Boondi Ke Laddu and the standards of Vanaspati cannot be applied to such a product particularly when the PA herself has admitted that BT Test might give negative result upon heating.
12. I have heard the arguments advanced by Ld. SPP for the complainant and Ld. Defence Counsel for the accused and have carefully perused the material available on record.
13. It is to be understood that the notice framed against the accused is for violation of section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of the PFA Act on the basis of CFL report.

Under section 2(ia)(a) of PFA Act, the prosecution has to establish that the purchaser had demanded a food article of a specific nature,
substance or quality and the article sold was, to his prejudice, either not of the nature, substance or quality demanded, or was not of the nature, substance or quality which it purported or represented to be.

On the other hand, section 2(ia)(m) of PFA Act deals with situation where the quality or purity of an article falls below the prescribed standard or its constituents are present in quantities not within the prescribed limits of variability which does not render it injurious to health.

3 14.

sentences.text: In the case at hand, it is an admitted position that Boondi Ke Laddu is not a standardized food article for which specific standards might be prescribed in any item of Appendix-B of the PFA Rules.

The same has been considered as a proprietary food as denied in Rule 37A of PFA Rules.
15.
The incriminating material on the basis of which the sample of Boondi Ke Laddu has been failed by the PA is the negative BT Test or Baudouin Test.
As stated by PW-4, this test is conducted to determine the presence of Til Oil in Vanaspati.
This is primarily to detect adulteration in Ghee and Vanaspati.
Apparently, such standard has been prescribed for Vanaspati as a food article falling under Item No. A.19 of Appendix-B of PFA Rules.
No such standards are there for Boondi Ke Laddu as a food article.
The question is as to what extent the standards of Vanaspati can be applied to such a proprietary food.
16. For a proprietary food, no standards could be possibly prescribed as every manufacturer uses his own ingredients, methods and substance and combination thereof to prepare a distinct product.
Unless there is violation of any prescribed rule, no standards are prescribed for such product on which they have to conform.
17. PW-4 PA categorically accepted that the sesamol content of Vanaspati gets degraded upon constant heating due to which the BT Test might be negative.
She also accepted existence of the standard literature in the Form of the book by David Pearson.

Ld. Defence Counsel has shown the said book titled as 'The Chemical Analysis of Foods', according to which BT Test is conducted to identify the sesame oil which is based on the presence of phenolic substance sesamol.
It is clearly mentioned that this substance is destroyed by heat and no reaction takes place with oils which have been heated for 30 minutes at 200 degrees.

18. With such clear evidence, it is apparent that the standards of Vanaspati as per Item No. A.19 would not be safe to be applied to all the products prepared through Vanaspati, particularly the proprietary foods that are prepared after heating the Vanaspati and roasting/frying the prime ingredient therein.
It is not the case of the prosecution that the Vanaspati used in preparation of Boondi Ke Laddu is the unheated Vanaspati which would always give a positive BT Test.
The stand taken by the accused is quite probable that to prepare Boondi Ke Laddu, the main ingredients are heated for frying in Vanaspati.
This fact is also admitted by PW-1.
In such a case, the phenol substance would get degraded and it is quite possible that BT test gets negative result in such position.
Therefore, there is nothing to show that there was any shortfall in the product on account of its nature, quality or substance.
The negative BT Test could have been only the result of heating of Vanaspati.
19 . There is nothing to show that the Vanasapti being used by the accused was not conforming to the standards.
The position might have been different had the FI lifted the sample of Vanaspati in which the boondi was to be fried for preparation of Laddus.
In that case, the standards of Vanaspati could have been applied.
But when the Vanaspati was heated constantly so as to fry the boondi, the negative BT Test would not be conclusive to say that there was any deficiency in the Vanaspati used in the same.
Therefore, merely because the BT Test was negative in case of a proprietary food, it would not qualify to bring the matter within the purview of Section 2 (ia)(a) of the PFA Act.

sentences.text: Similarly, since there are no standards prescribed for Boondi Ke Laddu, there would be no violation of Section 2(ia)(a) and (m) of PFA Act.
20. Having said so, the accused is entitled to be given benefit of doubt.
The prosecution has not been able to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt that the accused was selling and adulterated food article.
21. The accused is therefore acquitted of the charges.

However, his bail bonds shall remain in force for the next six months in terms of section 437-A. CrPC.
22.
File be consigned to record room.
